content:
Apple has detailed the extensive list of security patches included in the iOS 26.6, iPadOS 26.6 and related software updates.

The iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6 security updates impact iPhones and iPads in a number of ways

Apple has released more than 75 security fixes for iPhones and iPads in iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6, covering a number of areas of the system.

More specifically, Apple's advisory contains 78 separate vulnerability entries, involving 87 separate CVE identifiers. The higher CVE count is because some entries involve more than one CVE.

Apple does not indicate that any of the vulnerabilities fixed in iOS 26.6 were exploited in the wild.

There are several fixes on Apple's long list that stand out:

  • A vulnerability in MediaRemote could allow an app to gain root privileges.
  • A vulnerability in AVEVideoEncoder could allow an app to execute arbitrary code with kernel privileges.
  • Vulnerabilities in Game Center and libc could allow a malicious app to escape its sandbox.
  • A vulnerability in CloudAttestation could allow a malicious app to bypass code signing verification.
  • A vulnerability in ImageIO could result in arbitrary code execution when processing a maliciously crafted image.
  • Three vulnerabilities in SceneKit could result in arbitrary code execution when processing a maliciously crafted file.
  • An Accessibility issue could disclose sensitive information via iPhone Mirroring to someone with physical access.
  • A vulnerability in Contacts could allow an app to add contacts without user knowledge.

Kernel, WebKit and Wi-Fi fixes

Apple also patched more than a dozen kernel vulnerabilities. Potential impacts include corrupting or writing to kernel memory, leaking kernel memory, bypassing network filters, and causing the system to terminate unexpectedly.

WebKit also received a large number of fixes. The related vulnerabilities could leak process memory, expose whether a user has visited a particular link, spoof the interface, violate iframe sandbox rules, allow an app to read files outside its sandbox, or cause Safari to crash.

A separate Wi-Fi vulnerability could allow a nearby attacker to corrupt process memory.

Beyond the 78 documented security fixes, Apple also includes an "additional recognition" section listing 12 acknowledgments.

These are credits to people who assisted in the research, but are not separate security fixes and have not been assigned additional CVE identifiers.

The full list of patches and researcher credits is available on Apple's website.

Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV and Apple Vision Pro security fixes

Apple's newly published macOS Tahoe 26.6 security advisory lists 155 separate CVEs.

Beyond the many fixes shared with the iPhone and iPad, this Mac update also addresses vulnerabilities that could allow an app to gain root privileges, escape its sandbox, bypass Gatekeeper checks or privacy preferences, or access protected data.

Apple also released security updates for older versions of macOS today, which are not included in the count here.

Apple also published fixes for watchOS 26.6, tvOS 26.6 and visionOS 26.6. After accounting for overlap between platforms, the latest updates collectively address 194 separate CVEs.

Apple previously said it expedited some of the security fixes in last month's iOS 26.5.2 release due to the emergence of AI-powered attack tools.
